subject: Divergent transitions in ZIP model - only occurring with quadratic terms

messages.author: 91021b7b77105f99
messages.subject: Divergent transitions in ZIP model - only occurring with quadratic terms
parts:
Hi all,

I've just started learning Stan (2.14.2) as part of my first foray into Bayesian statistics. I'm implementing a zero-inflated Poisson model. I've attached the data, model, and R driver file.

The problem is as follows. Whenever I include a squared term as a predictor in either the Bernoulli or Poisson component, I get several hundred divergent transitions. This only occurs for squared terms, regardless of which term I use. The problem persists regardless of scaling predictors in advance. Parameter estimates make sense. Setting a bunch of control options does not get rid of the divergent transitions. I've checked the documentation, and this recommends reparameterization, which I do not understand at this point. I adapted the model code from Bayesian Data Analysis in Ecology using Linear Models in R, BUGS, and Stan (chapter 14 section 2).

Can someone tell me what I'm doing wrong?

Thank you,
Michiel Pillet

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Divergent transitions in ZIP model - only occurring with quadratic terms
parts:
Maybe it's related to numerical overflows, try this, for instance:


  logit_theta = a_0 + x_theta * a; 
  log_lambda = b_0 + x_lambda * b + offset_interval;
 
  // priors
  a_0~normal(0,100);
  a~normal(0,100); 
  b_0~normal(0,100);
  b~normal(0,100);

  // likelihood
  for (i in 1:N) {
    if(y[i] == 0)
      target += log_sum_exp(bernoulli_logit_lpmf(1 | logit_theta[i]),
                            bernoulli_logit_lpmf(0 | logit_theta[i]) + poisson_log_lpmf(y[i] | log_lambda[i]));
    else
      target += bernoulli_logit_lpmf(0 | log_theta[i]) +
                poisson_log_lpmf(y[i] | log_lambda[i]);
  }


You can the define theta and lambda in the generated quantities block if you'll need them.

I worked with ZIP and ZINB years ago, so I don't remember this very, but I remember there was an even more efficient way then the one about, at least for ZINB regression. I also wrote a Stan funcion for those two distributions zi_poisson_log_log and zi_neg_binomial_log (working directly on log/logit link functions), but never bother trying to merge this on Stan, I'll consider doing this now, since there seems to be some demand.

Also, if i remember well, the exposure of the Poisson does not have the expected properties on Zero inflated Poisson (i.e.: of producing the same inference as working with the individual Poisson terms), but I remember that there was some workarounds in literature, have you checked this?

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Divergent transitions in ZIP model - only occurring with quadratic terms
parts:
One potential problem becomes more evident if you write
the mixture model directly,

if (y[i] == 0)
target += log_sum_exp(log(theta[i]), log(1 - theta[i]) + poisson_lpdf(y[i] | lambda[i]);
else
target += log(1 - theta[i]) + poisson_lpdf(y[i] | lambda[i]);

log(inv_logit(…)) and log(1 - inv_logit(…)) can be numerically
unstable for large arguments, which would not be uncommon
given how diffuse your priors are.

Fortunately there are special functions that compute these values
in a much more numerically stable way,

vector[N] alpha = a_0 + x_theta * a;

if (y[i] == 0)
target += log_sum_exp(log_inv_logit(alpha[i]), log1m_inv_logit(alpha[i]) + poisson_lpdf(y[i] | lambda[i]);
else
target += log1m_inv_logit(alpha[i]) + poisson_lpdf(y[i] | lambda[i]);

You can go another step further by using the log-link variant of the Poisson,

vector[N] alpha = a_0 + x_theta * a;
vector[N] log_lambda = b_0 + x_lambda * b + offset_interval;

if (y[i] == 0)
target += log_sum_exp(log_inv_logit(…), log1m_inv_logit(…) + poisson_log_lpdf(y[i] | log_lambda[i]);
else
target += log1m_inv_logit(…) + poisson_log_lpdf(y[i] | log_lambda[i]);
